sections.h2: Where is Beaufort County, SC, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Beaufort County is a coastal Lowcountry county in the south of South Carolina, bordered by Colleton, Jasper and Hampton counties. Of its 923.48 square miles, 347.44 are water, about 37.6 percent, so rivers, creeks and the Atlantic shape where and how people build.

The county includes Hilton Head Island, Hunting Island, Daufuskie Island, Fripp Island, Lady's Island, Parris Island, Port Royal Island and Saint Helena Island. Its municipalities are Beaufort (the county seat), Bluffton, Hilton Head Island, Port Royal, and parts of Yemassee and Hardeeville. Hilton Head Island is the largest community.

A seller here may own a house on an island, near a marsh or in a planned community, and each of those can affect which tax district bills the property. The county auditor offers a Tax District Locator for that reason.

sections.h2: What is the history of Beaufort County?
sections.html:
The county dates to 1711 and is named for Henry Somerset, the 2nd Duke of Beaufort. Gullah culture and the Gullah language grew on the Sea Islands, where enslaved people made up a large share of the population.

Union troops occupied the area starting in 1861, and by March 1863 the Army had founded Mitchellville on Hilton Head, which had 1,500 residents by 1865. Beaufort County had prominent Black leaders in Reconstruction, among them Robert Smalls. Population fell from 35,495 in 1900 to 21,815 in 1930, then recovered as military bases and resort development drove growth in the second half of the 1900s.

sections.h2: How many people live in Beaufort County, and who employs them?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census counted 187,117 residents, up 15.3 percent from 162,233 in 2010, with about 76,373 households. A 2025 estimate puts the total at 204,433.

Accommodation and food services is the largest sector, at 19.6 percent of jobs, followed by retail at 16.1 percent and health care at 13.3 percent. Named major employers include the Beaufort County School District, Food Lion, Kroger, Marriott, Publix, the U.S. Department of Defense and Walmart. Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort and Parris Island give the northern end of the county a strong federal presence.

Resort and military work mean many houses change hands for job reasons, and a seller who is relocating often cares more about timing than about the last dollar.

US 278 is the main development corridor south of the Broad River, and SC 170 crosses the Broad River Bridge to connect the northern and southern halves of the county. Bluffton and Hilton Head Island sit on the southern side, while the city of Beaufort and Port Royal sit to the north.

That split is why the county runs two auditor offices, one at 100 Ribaut Road in Beaufort and one at 4819 Bluffton Parkway in Bluffton. Both are open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and on Wednesday they open at 9:00 a.m. in Beaufort and 10:00 a.m. in Bluffton.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Beaufort County?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work. The Auditor creates tax notices and applies the millage set by the county and municipalities, the Treasurer mails the notices and collects payment, and the Assessor values real property and handles the legal residence application.

  • Assessor: (843) 255-2400, 100 Ribaut Road, Room 210, Beaufort.
  • Auditor: (843) 255-2500, which also takes the senior homestead exemption for age 65 and older.
  • Treasurer: (843) 341-8404, with online payment at myBeaufortCounty.com.

The Treasurer also manages the installment program, delinquent taxes and tax sales, and posts a Tax Document Lookup where you can find original tax bills and paid receipts.

sections.h2: When are Beaufort County property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due January 15, and a payment postmarked after that date picks up statutory penalties. State law adds 3 percent after the due date, another 7 percent after February 1, and another 5 percent after March 16, and then the bill is turned over for execution.

The Treasurer's January 2026 notice warns that a postmark can show the processing date, not the day you dropped the envelope in the box. Staff can waive a penalty in limited cases, such as documented proof of timely USPS acceptance or a verified county error. The office suggests mailing several days early or asking a post office counter for a manual postmark.

If the property changed hands during the year and the buyer never got a notice, state law tells the treasurer to waive the penalties. The Assessor's guidance for a current-year sale is to forward the notice to the new owner or contact the closing attorney.

sections.h2: When does Beaufort County reassess, and how do you object?
sections.html:
The county's last reassessment took effect in 2023, and the Assessor's FAQ lists 2028 as the next one. State law requires a countywide reappraisal every fifth year.

The Assessor's Important Dates page sets out two ways to object to a value:

  • File between January 1 of the current year and January 15 of the following year.
  • Or file within 90 days of receiving an assessment notice.

The page adds that a taxpayer cannot use both options in the same tax year. After the assessor responds, state law gives 30 days to appeal to the county board of assessment appeals, and another 30 days after the board decides to ask for a hearing at the Administrative Law Court.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the assessment in Beaufort County?
sections.html:
A sale usually triggers an assessable transfer of interest, and the Assessor says the appraisal date for it is December 31 of the transfer year. A primary residence is taxed at 4 percent only when the owner applies, and the Assessor accepts 4 percent applications from January 1 of the current year through January 15 of the following year. Buyers who skip it are billed at 6 percent.

Beaufort County also publishes an ATI exemption that can reduce the fair market value by up to 25 percent, but not below the current county record value, with the property assessed at 6 percent for the year it is granted. Applications are due before January 31 of the tax year you first qualify. Ask the Assessor whether a particular sale qualifies.

sections.h2: What can a seller do with unpaid tax in Beaufort County?
sections.html:
You can sell the house and have the unpaid taxes paid at closing, which is usually cleaner than waiting for a tax sale. After a delinquent tax sale, the defaulting owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor has twelve months to redeem by paying the taxes, penalties and costs plus interest, which rises from 3 percent in the first quarter to 12 percent in the last.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Beaufort County houses as they are, including inherited homes and rentals, and the closing attorney handles the tax payoff. Send us the address and the latest notice, and we will review it with you.

faqs.q: When are Beaufort County, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15. A payment postmarked after that date is charged statutory penalties, so mail early or pay online at myBeaufortCounty.com.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about my Beaufort County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at (843) 341-8404 for payment, the Auditor at (843) 255-2500 for notices and homestead, and the Assessor at (843) 255-2400 for value or the 4 percent residence rate.

faqs.q: How soon should a Beaufort County buyer apply for the 4 percent rate?
faqs.a: Applications are accepted from January 1 of the current year through January 15 of the following year. A home not approved is billed at the higher 6 percent rate.

faqs.q: How long do I have to object to a Beaufort County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date of an assessment notice, or you can file from January 1 through January 15 of the following year. You cannot use both options in the same tax year.

faqs.q: When is the next Beaufort County reassessment?
faqs.a: The Assessor's FAQ lists 2028, with the most recent one in 2023. Check with the office, because the schedule can change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Beaufort County house with tax unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing attorney can pay the taxes and penalties from your proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff good through the closing date.
